name: DANCE
full_name: Dark matter Axion search with riNg Cavity Experiment
summary: A search for axion-induced polarization rotation using an optical ring cavity without an applied magnetic field.
detection_principle: An axion background produces a small periodic difference in the phase velocities of left- and right-circularly polarized light; a bow-tie cavity enhances the measurable rotation of linear polarization.

status.label: Prototype experiments / R&D
status.evidence: 2023 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: First results of axion dark matter search with DANCE

collaboration.name: DANCE Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

results.summary: DANCE Act-1 found no axion evidence and first validated cavity-polarization searches without an external magnetic field.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
